key_terms.meaning: For every action force there is an equal and opposite reaction force on a different body; these internal pairs cancel, so only outside forces change total momentum.
p = mv, mass × velocity in kg m s⁻¹; the total over an isolated system stays constant.
L = Iω for a rigid body about a fixed axis, in kg m² s⁻¹; constant when the net external torque is zero.
Force per unit area inside a deformed body, σ = F/A, unit N m⁻² = Pa.
Fractional change of size or shape, for example ΔL/L; a pure number with no unit.
Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L), the slope of the straight part of the stretching stress–strain graph, in Pa.
K = −P/(ΔV/V), resistance to uniform squeezing, in Pa; its reciprocal is compressibility.
σ = (Δd/d)/(ΔL/L), the sideways shrink per unit stretch, about 0.28 for steel.
The largest stress a body can take and still return exactly to its original shape when the load is removed.
The layer inside a bent beam that is neither stretched nor compressed, so its length does not change.
I_g = ∫y²dA over the cross-section, in m⁴; for a rectangle of breadth b and depth d, I_g = bd³/12.
δ = WL³/(3YI_g) for a beam fixed at one end with load W at the free end.
η = (F/A)/(dv/dx), shear stress per unit velocity gradient; unit Pa s, and 1 poise = 0.1 Pa s.
Drag on a small sphere in slow smooth flow, F = 6πηrv, with r the radius and v the speed.
v_t = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/(9η), the steady speed where weight = upthrust + viscous drag; ρ is sphere density and σ liquid density.
T = F/L, the force along a liquid surface per unit length of an imaginary line drawn on it, in N m⁻¹.
α = (1/L)(ΔL/ΔT), the fractional growth in length per kelvin; about 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ for steel.
σ = YαΔT, the stress produced when a rod is held at fixed length while its temperature changes by ΔT.
Two metals with different α welded face to face; unequal expansion makes the strip curl, so it can switch or indicate temperature.
γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²), always at least 1 and equal to 1 only for a body at rest.

takeaways: Newton's third law, read as a statement about pairs of internal forces, is exactly what makes momentum, energy and angular momentum conserved.
Every elastic modulus is a slope on the stress–strain graph and is meaningful only below the elastic limit.
How far a beam sags depends on the shape of its cross-section through I_g, not just on the amount of material.
Terminal velocity is the meeting point of three forces, and the formula rearranges to give η from a measured speed.
The drop weight method turns surface tension into a mass and a radius, needing only a chemical balance.
Blocking expansion converts a harmless length change into a stress YαΔT, which is why bridges have gaps and joints.
The same γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) produces both time dilation and length contraction.
At speeds below a few hundred km/s, γ differs from 1 by about v²/2c², far too small to see in ordinary engineering.
bank_note: Long answers here are usually marked on a clean chain of definitions, one full derivation with a labelled diagram, and a numerical whose units are carried through — and relativity questions almost always demand the derivation of time dilation or length contraction from the two postulates.

bank.q: State Newton's three laws of motion and show that the third law makes the total momentum of an isolated system constant.
outline: Clear statements of all three laws
Define system, internal force and external force
For one pair, F₁₂ = −F₂₁ so dp₁/dt + dp₂/dt = 0
Extend the sum to n particles
Note the laws hold only in an inertial frame

bank.q: Define stress and strain. Describe the three elastic moduli and Poisson's ratio, and give the relations connecting them.
outline: Longitudinal, shear and volume stress and strain with units
Y, G and K formulas from the slopes
Poisson's ratio definition and typical value for steel
Relations Y = 2G(1 + σ) and Y = 3K(1 − 2σ)
Regions of the stress–strain curve: proportional limit, yield, ultimate strength
One worked value for steel

bank.q: Explain the bending of a beam. Define the neutral surface and derive M = YI_g/R.
outline: Beam bends into an arc of radius R
Upper face stretched, lower face compressed, one layer unchanged
Strain at distance y from neutral surface = y/R
Stress = Yy/R, force on element = stress × dA
Moment about the neutral axis = (Y/R)∫y²dA = YI_g/R
State the assumptions: small bending, plane sections stay plane

bank.q: State Stokes' law and derive the terminal velocity of a sphere falling through a viscous liquid.
outline: Stokes' law with the conditions for its validity
Weight (4/3)πr³ρg down, upthrust (4/3)πr³σg up, drag 6πηrv up
Set the three forces to zero at steady speed
Obtain v_t = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/(9η)
Explain why v rises and then levels off, with a sketch

bank.q: State the postulates of special relativity and derive the time-dilation formula using a light clock.
outline: Two postulates stated exactly
Light clock with mirror separation L in the rest frame
Moving clock: light path = 2√(L² + (vΔt/2)²)
Equate cΔt to that path and solve
Δt = γΔτ; define proper time
Mention that each observer sees the other's clock slow

bank.q: A steel cantilever 1.0 m long, 2.0 cm wide and 1.0 cm thick carries a 2.0 kg load at its free end. Take Y = 2.0 × 10¹¹ Pa. Find I_g and the depression.
outline: I_g = bd³/12 with b = 0.02 m, d = 0.01 m, giving 1.67 × 10⁻⁹ m⁴
Convert load to weight W = 19.6 N
Use δ = WL³/(3YI_g)
Answer about 2.0 × 10⁻² m
Check that the stress stays below the elastic limit

bank.q: A steel ball of radius 1.0 mm and density 7800 kg m⁻³ falls steadily at 0.50 m s⁻¹ through a liquid of density 1200 kg m⁻³. Find η.
outline: Rearrange to η = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/(9v_t)
Substitute r = 1.0 × 10⁻³ m, ρ − σ = 6600 kg m⁻³
Answer about 2.9 × 10⁻² Pa s
Comment on the wall and end effects that spoil the result

bank.q: 50 water drops fall from a tube of internal radius 1.5 mm and together weigh 2.4 × 10⁻³ kg. Taking the drop-weight correction factor as 0.6, find the surface tension.
outline: Mass of one drop, then weight mg
Formula T = mg/(2πr f)
Substitute r = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m, f = 0.6
Answer about 8 × 10⁻² N m⁻¹
Compare with the accepted value for water and explain the gap

bank.q: A steel rod is clamped at both ends at 20 °C and heated to 60 °C. Given Y = 2.0 × 10¹¹ Pa and α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, find the thermal stress and the force on a 2.0 cm² cross-section.
outline: State that the rod cannot expand, so strain is forced to zero
σ = YαΔT with ΔT = 40 K
Answer 9.6 × 10⁷ Pa = 96 MPa
Force = σA with A = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ m², giving 1.9 × 10⁴ N
Nature of the stress: compressive on heating

bank.q: A rod of proper length 10 m moves at 0.8c along its length, and a particle of proper lifetime 2.2 μs moves at the same speed. Find γ, the measured length and the measured lifetime.
outline: L = L₀/γ = 6.0 m, contraction along the motion only
Δt = γΔτ = 3.7 μs
Stress that proper length and proper time are measured in the rest frame

bank.q: Why are bridge girders made with an I-shaped cross-section instead of a solid rectangle of the same mass? Use M = YI_g/R and δ = WL³/(3YI_g).
outline: Material near the neutral surface contributes little to I_g
Put most of the area far from the neutral axis, in the flanges
Same area, much larger I_g, so smaller stress and smaller sag
Depth enters as d³, so depth is more valuable than width
Thin webs can buckle locally, which sets a practical limit

bank.q: Explain how the Newtonian idea of an absolute frame was tested by Michelson and Morley, and what Einstein replaced it with.
outline: Galilean transformation and the assumed ether
Interferometer with two perpendicular paths, expected fringe shift on rotation
Null result, repeated at different seasons
Einstein's two postulates and the dropping of the ether
What becomes relative: simultaneity, length, time
The Newtonian limit at v much smaller than c

bank.q: Compare the terminal velocity method and the drop weight method as laboratory measurements of fluid properties, including their main sources of error.
outline: Principle and measured quantities in each
Stokes method errors: wall effect, non-sphericity, temperature drift, convection
Drop weight errors: evaporation, wetting of the tube, drop left on the tip
Corrections used in each case
Which suits a given liquid, and which is faster

bank.q: A 300 m steel bridge is erected at 20 °C and must survive 45 °C in summer. Discuss how expansion joints and girder cross-section both enter the design.
outline: If blocked, stress YαΔT ≈ 60 MPa
Expansion joints and bearings absorb the movement
Joints must not cut into the girder where I_g is needed
Bimetallic strips serve as the temperature sensors in such monitoring

bank.q: A rail or a pipe is fixed at both ends. Discuss whether it is safer to allow free expansion or to accept thermal stress, using numbers for steel.
outline: σ = YαΔT for complete restraint
Numerical value for a 40 K swing in steel
Buckling risk when hot, tensile cracking when cold
Use of gaps, loops and sliding bearings
Cost and maintenance comparison
Design choice depends on length and temperature range

glossary.def: The product of mass and velocity, p = mv, a vector in kg m s⁻¹.
Force multiplied by the time it acts, J = FΔt, equal to the change in momentum.
Turning effect of a force, τ = rF sinθ, in N m.
The point where the whole mass of a body may be taken to act for translation.
A frame of reference in which a body with no net force keeps a constant velocity.
The stress up to which stress is exactly proportional to strain, the straight part of the graph.
The stress at which the material suddenly stretches with little extra load.
The largest stress a material can carry before it breaks.
The ability of a material to be drawn out into a wire without breaking, shown by a long plastic region.
Energy stored in a stretched body per unit volume, ½ × stress × strain.
Deformation in which layers slide over each other, with no change of volume.
Smooth flow in parallel layers, with no mixing between them, the regime where Stokes' law applies.
Re = ρvd/η, the ratio of inertial to viscous forces; above about 2000 flow becomes turbulent in a pipe.
Buoyant force on a body in a fluid, equal to the weight of fluid displaced.
Liquid climbing a narrow tube to height h = 2T cosθ/(ρgr), where θ is the contact angle.
The angle between the liquid surface and the solid wall, measured inside the liquid at the line of contact.
A deliberate gap or sliding bearing in a structure that lets it change length without stress.
The time between two events measured in the frame where they happen at the same place; the shortest such time.
The length of an object measured in the frame in which it is at rest; the longest such length.
Two events happening at the same time; this is frame-dependent once moving frames are compared.
The algebraic rule connecting the coordinates of one inertial frame with another moving at speed v.
s² = c²t² − (x² + y² + z²), the same value in every inertial frame.
The energy a mass has even at rest, E₀ = mc².
A supposed all-pervading medium for light, which the Michelson–Morley experiment failed to detect.
A short-lived particle produced high in the atmosphere whose survival to ground level is evidence of time dilation.
